evidence.excerpt: This paper addresses the two-dimensional irregular strip packing problem, in which a set of non-convex polygonal pieces must be arranged within a fixed-width strip so as to minimise total strip length. A simulated annealing (SA) metaheuristic is implemented using no-fit polygon (NFP) calculations to evaluate feasible placements. The cooling schedule follows a geometric reduction with an initial temperature calibrated on 200 random placement trials per instance. Benchmark instances from the ESICUP repository with 25 to 197 pieces are used; the algorithm achieves an average material utilisation of 83.4%, improving the best-known solutions on four out of twelve instances. Computational time on a single-core 2.4 GHz processor ranges from 18 to 340 seconds depending on instance size and polygon complexity. Sensitivity analysis shows that NFP pre-computation accounts for 62% of total runtime, motivating future work on approximate NFP methods. The implementation is validated against a commercial marker-making system on a real denim fabric dataset of 48 pattern pieces.
